controls: Solid or gaseous biomass, or a bioliquid used for a non-energy purpose, is reported
Allow zero rating only for the qualifying biomass fraction.
Applying zero rating to the whole mixed stream
A GHGE permit holder uses a bioliquid to generate electricity, heating or cooling
Require retained verifier evidence that applicable sustainability criteria are met before zero rating.
An HSE permit holder reports a bioliquid biomass fraction
Apply the specific HSE route without requiring the main-scheme sustainability demonstration.
Applying main-scheme evidence rules to the HSE exception
An installation's UK ETS scope is assessed
Do not use biomass sustainability compliance to decide whether the installation is in scheme scope.
Excluding an installation because a fuel fails sustainability criteria
Evaluate land-use criteria and lifecycle GHG-emission-saving criteria as separate gates.
Collapsing two legal tests into one
A bioliquid is produced from waste or residue
Apply the land-use exemption only where the residue is not agricultural, aquaculture, fisheries or forestry residue.
A residue comes from agriculture, aquaculture, fisheries or forestry
Do not assume automatic compliance with land-use criteria.
Incorrectly zero-rating an excluded residue category
The applicable sustainability criteria are selected
Classify the bioliquid as waste, residue, product or co-product before applying criteria.
The operator claims the waste land-use exemption
Provide waste-status evidence such as an environmental permit or waste-transfer note to the verifier.
A substance was deliberately modified or contaminated to become waste
Exclude it from the waste definition used for the sustainability exemption.
A recognised voluntary scheme is used as sustainability evidence
Confirm that recognition covers the whole relevant supply chain and each applicable criterion.
Relying on a partial scheme certificate
One recognised scheme does not cover the full supply chain or both criteria
Allow multiple schemes to close the evidenced coverage gap.
Rejecting a valid combined evidence chain
Fuel is delivered in multiple consignments
Retain voluntary-scheme compliance evidence for every consignment.
Extrapolating one certificate to unevidenced fuel
No recognised voluntary scheme covers the bioliquid
Use an eligible default value, actual value or permitted combination of default and actual values.
Treating absence of a scheme as automatic failure or automatic pass
A RED default GHG value is proposed
Check that the pathway and circumstances permit that default rather than assuming every Annex value is usable.
Default or calculated GHG savings support zero rating
Retain evidence showing that the value and calculation were used correctly for verifier review.
Losing the audit trail for the savings claim
Tallow is combusted even though it may be solid at room temperature
Treat it as a bioliquid for UK ETS reporting.
Classifying tallow solely by room-temperature state
Treat category 1 as waste for the relevant sustainability route.
Applying product rules to category 1 material
Treat category 3 as a product, not waste.
Using waste defaults for category 3 material
Imported tallow lacks a category 2 or 3 label
Apply category 3 requirements to the unknown category.
Giving an imported unknown category a favourable assumption
Any ABPR category of tallow is assessed
Do not require land-use criteria because tallow is not obtained directly from land.
Category 1 or qualifying category 2 tallow oil generates onsite heat
Allow the UK ETS-specific 83% GHG-saving simplification only for the stated heat-use route.
Using the simplification outside its scope
Require verifier evidence that the tallow category qualifies.
Tallow oil is used for electricity, biofuel or biogas production
Determine actual GHG-saving values instead of using the heat-only 83% simplification.
Extending a heat-specific default to other uses
Bioliquid raw material comes from primary forest or high-carbon-stock land
Treat it as fossil and deny zero rating.
Apply the test to raw-material production land rather than substituting a generic supply-chain assessment.
A bioliquid mixture contains multiple consignments
Demonstrate the relevant sustainability criteria separately for each consignment.
A mass-balance chain of custody supports a mixture
Maintain the balance across the entire supply chain or collect equivalent consignment information.
Breaking traceability between origin and use
Biomass calculation factors will be used
Describe in the monitoring plan how emission factors, preliminary factors and biomass fractions are determined.
A mixed fuel or material has biomass content at least 97%
Permit an approved no-tier approach, including an energy-balance route, only within this threshold gate.
Using no-tier treatment below the threshold
The fossil-fraction emissions form a de-minimis or marginal source stream
Permit the applicable no-tier route while preserving source-stream classification evidence.
Determine calculation factors under the applicable Annex II tiers.
Applying the 97% simplification to a lower fraction
Tier 1 uses a default calculation factor
Put the value or an exact source reference in the monitoring plan.
A preliminary emission factor is stored
Represent total CO2 from fossil and biomass carbon before biomass-fraction adjustment, in the correct unit.
Confusing preliminary and final emission factors
Sustainability criteria apply but are not met
Set the qualifying biomass fraction to zero so the preliminary and final emission factors align.
A tier 3 preliminary factor is determined by analysis
Use the same analytical discipline applied to fossil fuels or materials.
Lowering analytical quality for biomass streams
A preliminary biomass factor is selected
Use an authorised source such as MRR Annex VI, the guidance table, IPCC guidance or the national inventory at its applicable tier.
Express biomass-origin carbon divided by total carbon as a fraction.
Using mass or energy share without an approved conversion
A mixed source stream receives zero rating
Apply it only to the biomass fraction and, where relevant, only the sustainable part of that fraction.
The operator cannot or chooses not to substantiate a biomass fraction
Allow the source stream to be treated fully as fossil.
A supported fossil/biomass mixture is reported
Multiply the preliminary factor by the fossil fraction for final emissions.
Counting the full preliminary factor after an evidenced biomass split
A mixed bioliquid claim lacks satisfactory sustainability evidence
Treat the whole source stream as fossil for compliance purposes.
Only part of a biomass mixture meets applicable criteria
Add the non-qualifying biomass part to the fossil fraction.
Biomass batches vary in sustainability evidence
Maintain a procedure assigning each batch to a sustainable-biomass or fossil source stream.
The highest tier is technically infeasible, unreasonably costly or tier 2 is regulator-approved
Use a documented estimation method only after satisfying one of those gates.
A biomass-fraction estimation method is selected
Use a scientifically proven method and prefer EN, ISO, national standards or peer-reviewed work.
A production process has defined and traceable input streams
Permit a mass balance of fossil and biomass carbon entering and leaving the process.
Applying mass balance without traceable inputs
Keep carbon mass balance distinct from the Article 38 energy-balance method.
Mixing two methods with different eligibility gates
Restrict it to mixed fuels or materials with biomass content at least 97% and do not use it to determine a lower biomass fraction.
Applying energy balance below its legal threshold
Either assume zero biomass or determine the fraction through compliant laboratory analysis.
Use an appropriate and current version of the relevant standard.
Using an obsolete or unsuitable method
BS EN ISO 21644 is used for solid recovered fuel
Recognise selective dissolution, manual sorting and radiocarbon as distinct methods with separate gates.
Treating all ISO methods as interchangeable
Use carbon-14 unless the regulator accepts unreasonable cost or technical infeasibility.
Choosing a weaker method without justification
A departure from carbon-14 is requested
Address correct sampling, sample preparation and suitably accredited carbon-14 analysis in the justification.
Selective dissolution or manual sorting is proposed
Validate the selected method against carbon-14 using several representative samples.
Require biomass content between 10% and 90% and the stated composition limits.
Using dissolution where the method is unreliable
Require particles over 10 mm and optically and physically distinguishable fractions that can be separated and quantified.
Using manual sorting on inseparable material
Highly variable solid waste is analysed
Design sampling and preparation to produce representative samples.
Treating a convenient grab sample as representative
An operator proposes the UK waste-tyre biomass fraction of 27.8%
Require regulator approval before using the industry-derived value.
The approved UK national waste-tyre factor is used
Do not apply a second biomass-fraction adjustment because the factor already includes it.
Biogas is injected into the natural-gas grid and the operator buys supplier certificates
Do not claim a matching biogas quantity in purchased natural gas solely from those certificates.
Peat, xylite or a fossil contamination is classified
Do not record it as biomass.
A listed biomass material contains varnish, resin, colour or another fossil contaminant
Treat it as mixed material and determine the qualifying fraction.
Treating contaminated material as pure biomass
A nominal biofuel contains fossil-origin intermediate carbon, such as fossil methanol in biodiesel
Treat the substance as mixed material rather than fully biomass.
